correctness_confidence.basis: All 36 published comparisons reduce to the claimed 24 profiles, all seven primal and dual objectives agree exactly, and the two quoted external-charge intervals are disjoint.

rigor.basis: The dual lower-bound argument is explicit. The 15-row accounting endpoint is disclosed; independent route geometry and a proof of uniqueness among routes are absent.

novelty.basis: The accounting rule is already public and minimax linear fitting is classical. The matched class table, numerical exclusion bounds and two-charge diagnostic add corridor-specific evidence.

significance.basis: For software quoting an exact corridor charge, the data distinguish two implementations. The maximum absolute discrepancies are small and consequences for actual invoices or route choices have not been measured.

reproducibility.basis: Two byte-identical PDF builds and the rational checker support replication. Reading the raw tariff annexes requires a separate extraction step; the short verifier works from transcribed data.

summary: The three-page PDF compares like-for-like truck classes across two published tariff tables. Fifteen section amounts recover each corridor total and exact signed-weight witnesses exclude seven aggregate fits at half-cent tolerance. The two-charge example isolates a stricter limit for displayed external-cost rates. This is a useful pricing-data validation for one Austrian corridor. I participated in the analysis and drafting and inspected all three rendered pages in shared context.
strengths: Complete coverage of the listed profiles and separate checking of duplicate Euro bands.
Exhibits attainable fits and lower witnesses rather than relying on optimizer output.
States prices excluding VAT and the different endpoint labels in the two documents.
weaknesses: One corridor and one tariff edition provide no out-of-area test.
The discussion would benefit from the official section identifiers or map that relates the named junction to the accounting endpoint.
The numerical effect on any real trip-selection decision remains unmeasured.
potential_errors: Counting all 36 comparisons as independent profiles exaggerates coverage.
The discrepancy for printed component rates does not determine the internal tariff calculation.
The 1.22 hypothetical detour does not identify a physically available alternative.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact corridor-specific uniform error floors for nested aggregate tariff models checked against the official section ledger.
